text:
ravi: quick flag from onboarding atlas-extended v1 int4q bring-up. seeing a small but repeatable KV misindex when RoPE rescale uses per-head multipliers and context crosses 48k. failing only on the quantized-tiled path. logs + repro below. :mag:

megan: can you paste the repro command and whether this is on staging or local?

ravi: staging (2xA100) tiled-int4 runtime. repro: 
```
python infra/run_infer.py --model atlas-extended-48k-int4q --quant int4-tiled --rope-rescale per-head \
  --context 49200 --prefill examples/legal_long.prefill --dump-kv /tmp/kv_atlas.json
```

ravi: log snippet:
```
[prefill] pos=49186
[generate] start pos=49186
[kv] page_map remap during prefill compaction
[kv] mismatch: key_pos=49184 expected_hash=0xab12 got=0xab11
[rebuild-kv] triggered -> latency bump
```

kai: that off-by-one in the hash at the very high context seems like index arithmetic when mixing per-head RoPE scale factors with tiled packing. did you run with TILE_OFFSET_WIDTH=16 vs 32?

ravi: quick test: set TILE_OFFSET_WIDTH=32 at runtime, mismatch disappears. repeating with `--rope-rescale=none` also passes, so it's an interaction between tiled offset width and per-head rescale math.

megan: opsbot, can you open an incident and add to the model onboarding checklist?

opsbot: created INC-2026-1503: "atlas-extended int4 tiled KV index off-by-one with per-head RoPE rescale at >48k context". Linked this thread and assigned to ravi.

kai: action items:
- ravi: open runtime PR to widen tiled offset type and add a unit test that prefills >48k and verifies kv key hashes are stable across quant profiles. include perf tradeoff notes.
- megan: add an onboarding eval step: longprefill kv-hash-consistency (32k/48k/64k) across fp16/int8/int4-tiled with rope variants.
- kai: run token-diff bench overnight fp16 vs int4-tiled (per-head rescale) and post token-level diffs + latency.

megan: note: if widening offsets is undesirable for memory, consider remapping compaction to update per-page base hashes instead of global index math. but widening is simpler and low cost for these models.

ravi: will open PR and link here. preliminary perf: TILE_OFFSET_WIDTH=32 adds ~0.8% KV meta RAM on atlas-extended config. acceptable for onboarding canary. :white_check_mark:

kai: thanks all, keeping an eye on the overnight runs. :coffee:
